page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 4 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor, this instance features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA-NI. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

In benchmark evaluations, the n4-highmem-4 demonstrates moderate single-core performance but exhibits limitations under multi-core workloads. Single-core CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, place the instance in the average tier, while multi-core performance falls into the lower quartile. Memory performance reflects a similar pattern; read and write bandwidth tests for large uncached blocks show lower-tier throughput, though static web serving throughput remains average at 7.0 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, single-threaded compression and decompression perform moderately, whereas multi-threaded decompression and database operations score in the lower 25% of tested systems.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highmem-4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense parallel processing. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions provides some acceleration for lightweight vector and matrix operations, such as small-scale LLM inference, where text generation for a 135M model reaches an average speed of 92.48 tokens/sec. However, the lower multi-core and memory bandwidth scores suggest a performance tradeoff for highly parallelized or memory-bandwidth-sensitive tasks.

This instance is best suited for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint relative to compute power, such as small-scale databases, caching layers, memory-intensive web serving, and lightweight data processing tasks.
